# F209: expiring misses across consumer caches

Adds the F209 case and deployed receipts; the existing notes “CPU attribution and profile limits”, “Bound visited work, not just returned values” and “Single-flight readiness: admission before task creation” already carry the general measurement, SQL-bound and task-admission rules. Read those rather than duplicating their doctrine here.

## New failure: a short miss can become a permanent consumer result

PR249 round1 R249-001: the adapter kept a missing transcript for30s, but PA refresh_sizes converted NotFound into CachedSize{tokens:None,stale:false}. CachedSize::fresh had no age limit. A whole turn could create a transcript and finish during that adapter miss; an idle PA read inside the miss then installed a completed unknown that never retried without later activity. The adapter's30s TTL did NOT bound the downstream result's staleness.

The shipped fix keeps NotFound stale/retryable on the PA's existing60s round. Unbound and Unsupported stay completed. Eligible fleet seats are deduplicated before size refresh: at most one PA status attempt per missing seat per round, no new timer or process. A truly missing Claude/OMP/Codex transcript can therefore incur one root walk per minute from this caller; Copilot uses an explicit path stat and never root discovery on that miss. Adapter cache hits within30s need no lookup; unrelated requesters can refresh the shared miss. Scope changes/target invalidation are not an unconditional forever rate guarantee.

Source: crates/unisphere/src/lib.rs (MISS_TTL, full StatusTarget key, miss check inside the per-seat lock, positive hit clears miss); crates/daemon/src/pa_presence.rs (NotFound stale=true). The real-adapter regression `an_idle_seat_read_during_a_kept_miss_is_sized_once_it_expires` creates a transcript during the miss, waits expiry, then observes the large-seat FYI on the next round with no activity. `a_kept_miss_answers_only_its_own_target_and_a_hit_clears_it` guards the target transition. Round2 PASS output `cefd015bd6dd266000d90d1585268b0bb6337a16`; exact artifact14492720598 at cbe6a01d verified both.

## Shipped cards projection: what remains after replay disappears

PR251 keeps {after,holds} per durable SeatId in AppState. Required Spine::all_matching_after uses the forced(seat,kind,seq) index and seq>after; EventBus and all implementations delegate. A per-seat async lock spans query/fold/commit. Decode/fetch failure leaves the old cursor/set intact. SQLite's single writer allocates AUTOINCREMENT seq inside the transaction, so no lower allocated seq can commit after a visible higher seq; generated payload finalization is in that same transaction. Durable SeatId semantics match the former full fold across rebind/revival; a cache reset alone would replay the same historical holds.

Only delivery replay became incremental: warm cards still make an indexed query per seat and clone returned holds. First successful card per seat/router lifetime still reads all matching history once (live earlier snapshot42,915 rows/120 seats). A delta clones the prior live set before commit. AppState.held is unpruned: O(ever-carded SeatIds + retained active holds), NOT current-live seats. Tombstones retain empty slots and any old active holds until daemon/router drop. Holds retain msg_id/reason/seat/since_ms, not message bodies; the BTreeMap key duplicates msg_id. No measured lifetime heap bound was established.

Final reviewed head6ed8f1f7acaba027db01e3cf47ffcbd697bed3d5; performance verdict1c083354. Exact-head JUnit artifact14492757970/run44444211355 passed the cold603/warm0/new1 row-counter regression, indexed cursor plan/result checks, stateful terminal/release ordering, no-tail cards and spawn_sites. No local builds/tests in this review seat.
